subject: Follow-up: request/response log handling and header masking for Greenline POC
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Moreno <amoren@greenlinehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: request/response log handling and header masking for Greenline POC

Hi Alicia — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and a few clarifying questions so we can scope the POC correctly: 

Summary from call:
- You will run live traffic through the Redwood hosted POC for 2 weeks (subset of users).
- Primary concerns: PII in request payloads, sensitive headers (cookies/authorization traces), trace IDs linking to internal user IDs, and retention windows for request/response logs.

Questions / asks for confirmation:
1) Which specific headers must never be persisted in any form? (list of header names is ideal)
2) Confirm desired retention for request/response logs (options we discussed: 7d, 30d, 90d).
3) Are trace IDs considered sensitive if they are correlated to user IDs on your side? Do you want us to pseudonymize or remove them?

What Redwood can provide (short):
- Option A: No request body retention (we only store token-level metadata + aggregated metrics).
- Option B: Request/response retention with real-time redaction rules (regex-based and header-level allowlist/denylist).
- Header masking: configurable to remove/replace values before write-to-disk.
- Trace IDs: can be hashed on ingestion or dropped entirely; we can also replace with a per-tenant pseudonym.

I attached two short artifacts: redwood_request_response_options.pdf (matrix of retention/masking combos) and header_masking_playbook.pdf (examples).

Proposed next steps:
- You confirm headers and retention choice by EOD Wed 6/18.
- If acceptable, we’ll put a short Statement of Work and a one-week security onboarding call (Marissa to lead the questionnaire).

Thanks — happy to jump on a short follow-up with security if helpful.

Best,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com | (415) 555-0192

From: Alicia Moreno <amoren@greenlinehealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: Greenline Security Team <sec@greenlinehealth.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Jun 2025 13:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: request/response log handling and header masking for Greenline POC

Hi Ben — thanks for the clear recap. A few specifics from our side to help you prepare the final options doc: 

1) Headers: please ensure the following headers are never retained in raw form: Authorization, Cookie, X-User-Id, X-Internal-Session. We may provide a longer list after the security intake.
2) Retention: for the POC we prefer 7-day retention, but for production Greenline requires a selectable retention up to 90 days with audit controls.
3) Trace IDs: these are currently correlated to user ids in our tracing pipeline. For the POC we want them pseudonymized (non-reversible hash) and for production we want the option to disable entirely.
4) Request bodies: small portions of request text will contain user-entered PII (names, limited SSNs). We need a redaction policy that can remove or obfuscate matching regex patterns before any long-term storage.

Also — are request/response logs accessible to Redwood support by default? We need role-based access controls so logs are only visible to our security ops and a redwood infra team during incident windows.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can:
- apply regex redactions in-flight and before any persistent storage;
- provide a digest (hash) of the raw payload for dedup/troubleshooting without storing the raw payload;
- and produce a list of who accessed logs and when (access audit trail) during the POC?

If you can confirm these points, we can move to SOW and schedule the onboarding call.

Thanks,
Alicia
Security Lead, Greenline Health
amoren@greenlinehealth.com

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Follow-up: request/response log handling and header masking for Greenline POC

Hi Alicia — good questions. Answers below (bullet per ask) and notes on what we need from you to finalize the POC config.

- Header retention: we can implement an ingestion-level denylist. The headers you listed (Authorization, Cookie, X-User-Id, X-Internal-Session) will be stripped and not written to persistent logs if configured. We recommend you provide the definitive header list in a single doc before enabling POC traffic.

- Retention windows: supported out of the box: 7d, 30d, 90d. For the POC we will set 7d by default; production options are configurable per-tenant and enforceable by policy.

- Trace IDs: we offer three options: 1) persist unchanged, 2) pseudonymize via HMAC (non-reversible with tenant key), 3) drop on ingestion. For your POC we can enable option (2) by default. This pseudonymized value is sufficient for debugging aggregated flows but cannot be used to reverse to your user IDs.

- Request body redaction: Redwood supports in-flight regex redaction and a set of built-in PII detectors (SSN, email, phone). Redaction is applied before persistence; raw payload is not stored if redaction rules match. We can also generate a SHA256 digest of the raw payload and discard the raw content — the digest is stored only if you opt-in.

- Access controls & audit: logs are role-based. By default, Redwood support does not have access to customer raw logs; access can be granted temporarily for troubleshooting with an entry in the audit log. We record access events (who/when/reason) and can export that as part of the POC deliverables.

What we need from Greenline to finalize the POC config:
- Definitive header denylist (file or spreadsheet)
- Confirmation to enable pseudonymized trace IDs (HMAC) for POC
- Confirmation whether you want the SHA256 digests stored for debug or not

I attached the two PDFs referenced in the earlier note. If this looks good I’ll have Marissa start the security onboarding questionnaire and we’ll draft the short POC SOW.

Subject: Re: Follow-up: request/response log handling and header masking for Greenline POC

Hi Alicia — looping in the security onboarding playbook. Thanks for the specific header list — that’s exactly what we need. Next steps from Redwood security side: 

1) I’ll send the short questionnaire (15–20 mins) targeted at configuration choices (headers, retention, trace-id treatment). Please have your security SME complete it prior to the onboarding call.
2) We’ll enable HMAC pseudonymization of trace IDs for the POC and set retention to 7 days unless you request otherwise.
3) We will not retain Authorization/Cookie headers; we will apply regex redaction to request bodies before any persistence.

Deliverables we’ll provide within the POC:
- Config manifest for the POC (retention + header denylist + trace policy)
- Exportable audit log of access events
- Short runbook for incident access requests

Proposed scheduling: 30-min security onboarding on Wed 6/18 at 10am PT. If that works I’ll send a calendar invite and a DocuSign link for the POC SOW.

Thanks — Marissa
